clue.text: Nut on old haulage vehicle that diverts unwanted emissions

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the enthusiast comes after the old vehicle

parts.note: ex- means former, old
a tractor hauls trailers and loads
a nut is an enthusiast, a fan

explanation.surface: A mechanic tightens a nut on a vintage lorry that is belching fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' looks like a bolt fitting on the lorry, but it is a fan, an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen or bathroom appliance that pulls steam, smoke and smells out of a room.

clue.text: Put out message in clubs — opening time delayed as late as possible

indicators.note: the opening letter of the built word is the one that moves
putting something off to the last moment sends that letter to the very end

parts.note: a text is a phone message
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A notice in nightclubs announcing that opening hours have been pushed back to the latest possible moment.
explanation.walkthrough: TEXT IN C gives TEXTINC; its opening T (time) is moved to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Put out as of a fire or a light: extinguished, no longer burning.

clue.text: Great Scott, finally everybody is together

indicators.note: together signals the two pieces are joined side by side
finally points to the last letter of the name Scott

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise, 'Great Scott!', as everyone finally gathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Scott' looks like one phrase, but Great is the definition and Scott only gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Great in the sense of large in height or size, as a tall tree is a great one.

clue.text: One misses ball bearings recently stolen

parts.note: airs are manners or bearings, how one carries oneself
hot goods are recently stolen ones

explanation.surface: Someone misses a party because the ball bearings they had were stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball bearings' reads as one engineering term, but 'ball' ends the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf or cricket a swing that fails to make contact with the ball is called by this name.

clue.text: Technique in court smart — moral flaw overturned

indicators.note: overturned in a down answer means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to smart or nip is to sting
a spot is a stain or blemish on one's character

explanation.surface: A tennis lesson praising smart technique, with a lapse of character upended.
explanation.walkthrough: Spelt from the bottom up: NIP SPOT reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: On a tennis court, spin applied by striking over the top of the ball so it dips and kicks forward.

clue.text: Run one?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one run, a contest of speed

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'one' stands for an example of the first word, a run.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to sprint; as a noun it is a competitive event over a set distance.

clue.text: Wild money-changing securing bric-a-brac

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: agio is the charge or premium for changing money
tat is cheap bric-a-brac

explanation.surface: A frantic moneychanger snatching up junk at a market stall.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction, Italian for agitated, played in a restless, excited manner.

clue.text: They may serve general support duties. That's about right

parts.note: a staff is a stick for support

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the duties word goes round the letter

parts.note: offices are duties or functions

explanation.surface: A description of soldiers who support a general in their duties, followed by an approving remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like an adjective with 'support', but it is the army rank being served.
explanation.definitionFit: Military officers attached to a commander's staff who assist with planning and administration.

clue.text: What could be generated by working rickety engine

definitions.text: What could be generated by working rickety engine

indicators.note: working means operating or being worked, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Physics: a rattling engine in motion produces energy of motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy of motion is what any running engine, however shaky, produces as its parts move.

clue.text: Awful unbridled brutality of a 26 for one

indicators.note: awful signals the letters are messed into a new order
unbridled means without its outer edges, so only the inside of the word brutality stays

explanation.surface: Condemns the savage cruelty of some aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is LORD, so the definition reads 'of a lord, for example', a title-holder. Dropping B and Y leaves RUTALIT to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Titular means relating to a title, which a lord holds as a nobleman's rank.

clue.text: Composer in Italy in court taken aback about copied email

indicators.note: about means going round, so the reversed letters enclose the copy marker
taken aback means turned backwards, so the run is read in reverse

parts.note: the first in is taken as written
I is the international car code for Italy
someone up before a judge is in court
cc, carbon copy, marks a copied email

explanation.surface: A composer facing trial in Italy is dismayed by an email he was copied in on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' for 'in court' is the British sense of being up before the magistrate; 'cc' is the carbon-copy line of an email.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Puccini wrote the operas La Bohème, Tosca and Madama Butterfly.

clue.text: Subtle condition back in place at last

indicators.note: back means the word for condition is reversed

parts.note: if introduces a condition

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of each of in and place

explanation.surface: Someone whose condition is quietly improved now they are home at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine as in delicate and nuanced, as a fine distinction is a subtle one.

clue.text: Sends off second half of suits

indicators.note: second half of keeps only the back half of the word, dropping its first half

parts.note: suits in the sense of wooings, courtships

explanation.surface: Someone dispatching the remaining half of a batch of suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits' looks like clothing, but it is the old sense of wooing.
explanation.definitionFit: To ship goods is to dispatch or send them off.

clue.text: Fashion magazine covers article 1,000 inside

indicators.note: inside means the article and thousand go within the covers
covers means just the outside letters of the word magazine

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A fashion magazine whose pages include an article and a thousand items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion magazine' reads as one phrase, but Fashion is the verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fashion something is to make or shape it.

clue.text: Laugh about grabbing tense canine, for one

indicators.note: grabbing means the reversed laugh holds the letter within
about means the word for laugh is turned round

parts.note: a hoot is a laugh
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone laughing while grabbing a nervous dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' looks like a dog, but here it is the pointed tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is the pointed tooth beside the incisors, one example of a tooth.

clue.text: Chief investigator ultimately cracking handwriting

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: fist is an informal word for handwriting

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of investigator

explanation.surface: A senior detective finally deciphers a piece of handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief investigator' reads as one title, but Chief alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: First as in foremost or principal, the top position.

clue.text: In error after division that's nowhere near?

parts.note: out means wrong, as in your sums are out
post means after, as in post-war

explanation.surface: A mistaken calculation after a long division sum, nowhere near the right answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'division' looks arithmetical, but it is a military detachment stationed far away.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote station or detachment of troops posted far from the main body.

clue.text: New fetish fuelled by publicity somewhere in Africa

indicators.note: fuelled by puts the publicity word before the fetish word

parts.note: air as in giving something airtime, publicity
obi is a West Indian form of sorcery or a charm, a fetish

explanation.surface: A new craze driven by media hype somewhere on the African continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya in East Africa.

clue.text: A lot of rubbish by experienced writer

parts.note: felt means experienced, as felt pain
a tip is a rubbish dump, holding a lot of rubbish

explanation.surface: A seasoned author dismissed as producing mostly trash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' looks like an author, but it is a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen with a fibre point, a writing implement.

clue.text: Try getting album released up-front — a pain

indicators.note: up-front means the rearranged letters sit ahead, above in a down answer
released means freed up, so the letters of album come loose and rearrange

parts.note: a go is a try

explanation.surface: A musician tries to get an album out early, which proves a hassle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the lower back.

clue.text: Examiner for each employer

parts.note: per means for each
a user is one who employs something

explanation.surface: An inspector assigned to every company boss.
explanation.definitionFit: One who peruses reads through and inspects something carefully.

clue.text: Potential charge for throwing party one held?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a playful coinage, like postage for posting, a fee for hosting
second meaning: a captive kept as security

explanation.walkthrough: The first half invents a word: as postage is a charge for posting, this would be a charge for hosting a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A person seized and kept prisoner to force others to meet demands.

clue.text: Make citizen's arrest of old woman grabbing girl over ring

indicators.note: grabbing means the hag holds the reversed name within

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman

indicators.note: over in a down answer means the name is read upwards

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An old woman grabs a girl and her ring, prompting a bystander to stop her.
explanation.walkthrough: To have a go is a British idiom for tackling a criminal oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander who tackles a thief is said to attempt the detention themselves.

clue.text: Shellfish muscle unique

parts.note: abs, abdominal muscles; one is an ab
alone means unique, the only one

explanation.surface: Praise for a shellfish of singular strength.
explanation.definitionFit: An abalone is an edible sea mollusc with an ear-shaped shell lined with mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Company with Marx Brothers' heads for crest

indicators.note: heads means the first letters of Marx and Brothers

explanation.surface: A comedy troupe teams up with the Marx Brothers to top the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A comb is the fleshy crest on top of a cockerel's head.

clue.text: Extremely poor climber's secret

indicators.note: extremely points to the outermost letters of poor

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant; climber's means climber is

explanation.surface: A poor mountaineer's hidden secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Privy to a secret means sharing private knowledge; privy means private, secret.

clue.text: Worthless singer on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard over the airwaves, by sound only

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced singer

explanation.surface: A poor vocalist dismissed after a broadcast performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means low in value or morals, as base metals are of little worth.

clue.text: Briefly jest about master

indicators.note: about means the shortened word is turned round
briefly means cut short, dropping the final letter

parts.note: a droll is an old word for a jester or a jest

explanation.surface: A servant makes a quick joke about the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: DROLL less its last L is DROL, then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord is a master, a ruler with authority over others.

clue.text: Animal impression

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a marine mammal with flippers
second meaning: a mark stamped into wax

explanation.walkthrough: 'impression' suggests mimicry, an animal impersonation, but it is the stamp pressed into wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A flippered marine mammal, and the imprint made by a stamp or signet.

clue.text: Make right start to periods of play in football grounds

indicators.note: make tells us to turn the start into something else
start to points at the opening letter, which is the one replaced

parts.note: football is played in seasons

explanation.surface: Instructions to sort out how matches begin at football stadiums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'football grounds' looks like stadiums, but grounds alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds for an action are the reasons or justification behind it.

clue.text: Lasting throughout, say, withdrawn inside

indicators.note: inside means the reversed letters go within

parts.note: along means throughout, as all along

indicators.note: withdrawn means pulled back, so the abbreviation reads backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A remark that someone remained reserved and introverted all along.
explanation.definitionFit: Agelong means lasting for an age, for a very long time.

clue.text: One participating in round-up about Suffolk or Lincoln?

definitions.text: One participating in round-up about Suffolk or Lincoln?

parts.words: One participating in round-up about Suffolk or Lincoln?
parts.note: Suffolk and Lincoln are breeds of sheep, so the round-up is a sheepdog herding them; the surface suggests a news summary about places

explanation.walkthrough: Suffolk and Lincoln look like English counties or cities in a news round-up, but both are sheep breeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of sheepdog from the Anglo-Scottish borders, used to herd flocks.
